newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Lower House approves re-election amendment.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Lower House approves re-election amendment.

text.p: Brazil's Lower House voted on Tuesday to approve a constitutional amendment allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to seek an unprecedented second term in office.

The amendment, which still requires a second round Lower House vote and Senate approval, was approved by 336 deputies, 17 voted against and six abstained according to Lower House president Luiz Eduardo Magalhaes.
The amendment paves the way for Cardoso, who is halfway through a four-year term, to run in the 1998 presidential election.
It would also allow state governors and mayors to run for a second consecutive term.
Brazil has banned re-election since the founding of the Republic in 1889.
The Lower House was due to vote on Wednesday morning on a series of proposed alterations to the bill floated by opposition parties.
